metadata.title: Distribution of Eigenvalues for Some Sets of Random Matrices
metadata.authors: V. A. Marchenko and L. A. Pastur
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Random selfadjoint operator $B_N(n)$
nodes.statement: $B_N(n) = A_N + \sum_{i=1}^{n} \tau_i (\,\cdot\,, q^{(i)}) q^{(i)}$, where $A_N$ is a nonrandom selfadjoint operator on the $N$-dimensional unitary space $H_N$, the $\tau_i$ are i.i.d. real random variables, and the $q^{(i)}$ are mutually independent random unit vectors in $H_N$, independent of the $\tau_i$.
nodes.statement_clean: The random Hermitian operator studied is the sum of a nonrandom selfadjoint operator and n independent rank-one perturbations.

nodes.name: Normalized spectral function
nodes.statement: $\nu(\lambda; B_N(n))$ is the ratio of the number of eigenvalues of $B_N(n)$ lying to the left of $\lambda$ to the dimension $N$ of the space; it is a nondecreasing left-continuous piecewise-constant function of $\lambda$ with $0 \le \nu(\lambda; B_N) \le 1$.

nodes.name: Concentration $c$
nodes.statement: $c = \lim_{N \to \infty} n/N$, called the concentration parameter relating the number of rank-one perturbations to the dimension.

nodes.name: Stieltjes transform $m(z; c)$
nodes.statement:
$m(z; c) = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty}  rac{d
u(\lambda; c)}{\lambda - z}$, with inversion $
u(\lambda_2; c) - 
u(\lambda_1; c) = \lim_{\eta 	o +0}  rac{1}{\pi} \int_{\lambda_1}^{\lambda_2} \mathrm{Im}\, m(\xi + i\eta; c)\, d\xi$.

nodes.name: Generalized inverse $\tau(\xi)$
nodes.statement: $\tau(\xi) = \inf\{\tau : \sigma(\tau) \ge \xi\}$, the generalized inverse of the probability distribution function $\sigma(x)$ of the random variable $\tau$.

nodes.name: Empirical distribution $\sigma(x, T_n)$
nodes.statement: For a realization $T_n = \{\tau_1 \le \ldots \le \tau_n\}$, $\sigma(x, T_n) = 0$ for $x \le \tau_1$, $i/n$ for $\tau_i < x \le \tau_{i+1}$, and $1$ for $\tau_n < x$. Its inverse $\tau(\xi, T_n)$ is defined by $\tau(\xi, T_n) = \tau_{i+1}$ for $i/n < \xi \le (i+1)/n$.

nodes.name: Conditions I-IV on $A_N$, $q^{(i)}$, $\tau_i$
nodes.statement: (I) The limit $\lim_{N \to \infty} n/N = c$ exists. (II) $\lim_{N \to \infty} \nu(\lambda; A_N) = \nu_0(\lambda)$ at all points of continuity. (III) The $q^{(i)}$ have moments through fourth order satisfying $M q_i \bar q_j = N^{-1}\delta_{ij} + a_{ij}(N)$ and a fourth-moment factorization with vanishing remainders. (IV) The $\tau_i$ are i.i.d. with common distribution $\sigma(x)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Standing assumptions: convergence of the concentration n/N to c; convergence of the empirical spectrum of A_N; second- and fourth-moment conditions on the random vectors q; i.i.d. random coefficients tau.

nodes.name: Marchenko-Pastur theorem (main result)
nodes.statement:
Under conditions I-IV: (1) $
u(\lambda; B_N(n))$ converges in probability to a nondecreasing function $
u(\lambda; c)$ at all points of continuity, with the same total mass as $
u_0$. (2) Its Stieltjes transform $m(z; c) = u(z, 1)$ where $u(z, t) = m_0(z) - c \int_0^t  rac{	au(\xi) u(z, \xi)}{1 + 	au(\xi) u(z, \xi)\, z}\, d\xi$. (3) The solution exists and is unique.
nodes.statement_clean: The empirical spectral measure of B_N(n) converges in probability to a deterministic limit nu(lambda; c) whose Stieltjes transform satisfies a fixed-point integral equation, with existence and uniqueness.
assumptions: $A_N$ is a nonrandom selfadjoint operator on $H_N$
conclusions: $\nu(\lambda; B_N(n)) \to \nu(\lambda; c)$ in probability at all continuity points
The Stieltjes transform $m(z; c)$ solves the integral equation $u(z, t) = m_0(z) - c\int_0^t \frac{\tau(\xi) u(z, \xi)}{1 + \tau(\xi) u(z, \xi)\, z} d\xi$ at $t = 1$
The solution to this equation exists and is unique
nodes.notes: Some signs/symbols in the integral kernel may be slightly garbled in the OCR text; the form follows the canonical Marchenko-Pastur master equation.

nodes.name: Master equation for $m(z; c)$
nodes.statement: $m(z; c) = -\Big(z - c \int \frac{\tau\, d\sigma(\tau)}{1 + \tau\, m(z; c)}\Big)^{-1}$ (eq. (1.14)), the implicit equation that the limiting Stieltjes transform satisfies.

nodes.name: PDE form of master equation
nodes.statement: $\frac{\partial u(z, t)}{\partial t} - c \frac{\tau(t) u^2}{1 + \tau(t) u(z, t)} = 0$, $u(z, 0) = m_0(z)$ (eq. (1.12)); the integral equation rewritten as a first-order PDE solvable by characteristics.

nodes.name: Spectrum-edge relation $x(m; c)$
nodes.statement: $x(m; c) = -1/m + c \int \frac{\tau\, d\sigma(\tau)}{1 + \tau\, m}$ (eq. (1.15)); the inverse of the Stieltjes transform restricted to intervals where it is monotone, used to locate spectrum boundaries.

nodes.name: Spectrum-boundary determination rule
nodes.statement: Procedure to locate the spectrum and its edge singularities of $\nu(\lambda; c)$ via the inverse function $x(m; c)$ of (1.15): identify intervals of monotonicity, take their image as the spectrum complement, and read off edge singularity exponents from local-extremum Taylor expansions.
output: The connected components of the spectrum of the limit measure $\nu(\lambda; c)$
Algebraic singularity exponents of the density $d\nu/d\lambda$ near boundaries

nodes.name: Form $x(m; c)$ from (1.15)
nodes.statement: Compute $x(m; c) = -1/m + c \int \frac{\tau\, d\sigma(\tau)}{1 + \tau\, m}$ as the candidate inverse of the Stieltjes transform on real intervals outside the spectrum.

nodes.name: Locate intervals of monotone increase
nodes.statement: Find the maximal real intervals on which $x(m; c)$ is monotonically increasing in $m$; the union of their images is the complement of the spectrum on $\mathbb{R}$.

nodes.name: Read off edges and singularity exponents
nodes.statement: At each endpoint $a$ of a monotonicity interval, $\lambda_a = x(a; c)$ is a spectrum boundary; from the order $2k$ of the first nonvanishing derivative of $x(m; c) - \lambda_a$ at $a$, read off the algebraic singularity exponent $1/(2k)$ in the density via (1.17).

nodes.name: Sum of random independent equiprobable projections
nodes.statement: Let $B_N(n) = \tau \sum_{i=1}^n P_i$ with $\tau$ a constant and $P_i$ projections onto i.i.d. uniform unit vectors $q^{(i)}$. Then $m(z; c)$ solves a quadratic, giving the explicit limit density supported on $[\tau(1-\sqrt{c})^2, \tau(1+\sqrt{c})^2]$ (plus an atom at $0$ when $c < 1$); as $c \to \infty$ one recovers Wigner's semicircle law.
nodes.notes: This is the canonical Marchenko-Pastur density.

nodes.name: Projections with bounded random coefficients
nodes.statement: Let $B_N(n) = \sum_{i=1}^n \tau_i P_i$ with $\tau_i$ i.i.d. with density $[\pi(1-\tau^2)^{1/2}]^{-1}$ on $(-1, 1)$. The master equation gives a cubic for $m$; for $c = 1$ it reduces to a biquadratic and yields an explicit density supported on $[-2, 2]$.

nodes.name: Projections with Cauchy-distributed coefficients
nodes.statement: Let $B_N(n) = \sum_{i=1}^n \tau_i P_i$ with $\tau_i$ Cauchy distributed with density $\pi^{-1} a/(a^2 + \tau^2)$. Then equation (1.14) becomes $m = -[z(1 - iac/(1 - iam))]^{-1}$, and the resulting limit spectrum occupies the entire real axis, as expected from unboundedness of $\tau$.

nodes.name: Quadratic-form concentration
nodes.statement: If the random vector $q = (q_1, \ldots, q_N)$ obeys condition III, then $M\,|(Aq, q) - N^{-1}\,\mathrm{Sp}\,A| \le \|A\|\, \varepsilon(N)$, where $\varepsilon(N)$ does not depend on $A$ and $\varepsilon(N) \to 0$ as $N \to \infty$.
assumptions: $A$ is a linear operator on $H_N$ with norm $\|A\|$
$q$ obeys condition III on second and fourth moments

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1
nodes.statement: Bounds the variance of the quadratic form $(Aq, q)$ by combining the second-moment identity $M(Aq, q) = N^{-1}\mathrm{Sp}\,A + O(\|A\| \varepsilon_1)$ with the fourth-moment estimate from (1.5)-(1.6) and the trace inequality $\sum |A_{ij}|^2 \le N \|A\|^2$.

nodes.name: Resolvent-trace difference under rank-one perturbation
nodes.statement: If Hermitian $\tilde A = A + \tau(\,\cdot\,, q)q$ with $q$ obeying III, then for the resolvents $R_z, \tilde R_z$, $\mathrm{Sp}\,\tilde R_z - \mathrm{Sp}\,R_z = -\frac{d}{dz} \ln[1 + \tau (R_z q, q)] + \delta(z, q, N)$, with $M|\delta(z, q, N)| \le |y|^{-1}\,\varepsilon(N)$ for $z = x + iy$.
assumptions: $A, \tilde A$ Hermitian with $\tilde A - A = \tau(\,\cdot\,, q)q$
conclusions: Trace-difference identity above with controlled error $\delta(z, q, N)$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: Uses the determinant identity $\det[I + R_z(\tilde A - A)] = 1 + \tau(R_z q, q)$ to derive the trace-difference formula, then bounds the random remainder via the resolvent norm $\|R_z\| \le |y|^{-1}$ and Lemma 1.

nodes.name: $L^1$ convergence of empirical inverse $\tau(\xi, T_n)$
nodes.statement: If $\sigma(x)$ has finite first absolute moment, then almost surely $\int_0^1 |\tau(\xi, T_n) - \tau(\xi)|\, d\xi \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3
nodes.statement: Combines Glivenko's theorem (uniform a.s. convergence of $\sigma(x, T_n)$ to $\sigma(x)$) with a truncation argument and the strong law of large numbers to bound the integral on neighborhoods of the endpoints $0, 1$.

nodes.name: Convergence of $u(z, \xi; N, T_n, Q_n)$ to integral equation
nodes.statement: Under I-IV and bounded $|\tau_i| \le T$, on any bounded set $G$ in $\{\mathrm{Im}\, z > 3T\}$, $M\,\varphi_N \to 0$, where $\varphi_N = \sup_{\xi \in [0, 1], z \in G}\big| u(z, \xi; N, T_n, Q_n) - m_0(z) + c \int_0^\xi \frac{\tau(l) u(z, l; N, T_n, Q_n)}{1 + \tau(l) u(z, l; N, T_n, Q_n)\, z}\, dl \big|$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4
nodes.statement: Builds the chain of operators $B_N(i) = A_N + \sum_{\alpha=1}^i \tau_\alpha (\,\cdot\,, q^{(\alpha)}) q^{(\alpha)}$, applies Lemma 2 to each rank-one increment, replaces $\tau(\xi, T_n)$ by $\tau(\xi)$ via Lemma 3, and uses compactness of $\{u\}$ and $\{u_z'\}$ to pass from pointwise convergence to uniform convergence on $G$.

nodes.name: Construct chain $B_N(i)$
nodes.statement: Order the $\tau_i$ in increasing order and set $B_N(i) = A_N + \sum_{\alpha=1}^i \tau_\alpha (\,\cdot\,, q^{(\alpha)}) q^{(\alpha)}$ with resolvents $R_z(i)$, defining $u(z, \xi; N, T_n, Q_n) = N^{-1}\mathrm{Sp}\,R_z(i) + n N^{-1}\mathrm{Sp}(R_z(i+1) - R_z(i))(\xi - i/n)$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 2 to consecutive resolvents
nodes.statement: Use Lemma 2 on $R_z(i+1)$ and $R_z(i)$ (which differ by a rank-one perturbation $\tau_{i+1}(\,\cdot\,, q^{(i+1)}) q^{(i+1)}$) to express the increment as $-(\tau_{i+1}/N)(R_z^2(i) q^{(i+1)}, q^{(i+1)})/(1 + \tau_{i+1} N^{-1}\mathrm{Sp}\,R_z(i)) + N^{-1}\delta_i(z, q^{(i+1)}, N)$ with controlled error.

nodes.name: Replace $\tau(\xi, T_n)$ by $\tau(\xi)$ via Lemma 3
nodes.statement: Combine the per-step identity into a discrete integral, use Lemma 3 to replace $\tau(\xi, T_n)$ by $\tau(\xi)$ in the $L^1$ sense, and pass to a continuous integral with controlled error.

nodes.name: Pointwise to uniform via $\varepsilon$-net
nodes.statement: Use the equicontinuity and uniform boundedness of $\{u, u_z'\}$ on $G \times [0, 1]$ to upgrade pointwise expectation convergence into uniform convergence over $\xi \in [0, 1]$ and $z \in G$.

nodes.name: Uniqueness of solution to limit integral equation
nodes.statement: Equation $u(z, t) = m_0(z) - c \int_0^t \frac{\tau(\xi) u(z, \xi)}{1 + \tau(\xi) u(z, \xi)\, z}\, d\xi$ has at most one solution in the class $K(\tau, z_0, R)$ of functions continuous in $(z, t)$, holomorphic in $z$ on $|z - z_0| < R$, and satisfying the bound (3.18).
assumptions: Two candidate solutions $u_1, u_2$ in $K(\tau, z_0, R)$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5
nodes.statement: Adapts Haar's contradiction argument: on a maximal cone $\xi_0 < t < \xi_0 + H$ where the difference $v = u_1 - u_2$ would be nonzero, exhibits a maximum of $e^{-2Lt}|v(z, t)|$ at an interior point $z_1, t_1$, then constructs perturbations $z_1 - \alpha s$ that violate the maximum modulus, contradicting the assumption $\xi_0 < 1$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: First treats bounded $\tau_i$: combines Lemma 4 (convergence of $u_N$ to a solution of the integral equation) with Lemma 5 (uniqueness) to get convergence in probability of $\nu(\lambda; B_N(n))$ to the deterministic $\nu(\lambda; c)$. Then lifts boundedness via truncation and Glivenko's theorem (Section 5).

nodes.name: Bounded-$\tau$ case via Lemma 4
nodes.statement: Under (3.0) $|\tau_i| \le T$, Lemma 4 yields a subsequence of $u(z, t; N, T_n, Q_n)$ converging uniformly to some $u(z, t)$ that satisfies the integral equation.

nodes.name: Identify limit via Lemma 5 uniqueness
nodes.statement: By Lemma 5 every limit point of $u(z, t; N, T_n, Q_n)$ is the same function $u(z, t)$, so the full sequence converges in probability; the inversion formula gives convergence in probability of $\nu(\lambda; B_N(n))$ to $\nu(\lambda; c)$.

nodes.name: Tail control via spectral inequality (4.13)
nodes.statement: Use the operator inequality $A_N - lI - D_2 \le B_N(n) \le A_N + lI + D_2$ together with the Chebyshev bound on $1 - N^{-1}\mathrm{Sp}\,E(l)$ to control the relative number of eigenvalues escaping to $\pm\infty$, yielding (4.6).

nodes.name: Truncation argument for unbounded $\tau$
nodes.statement: For arbitrary $\tau_i$, define truncated $\tau_i^T = \tau_i \mathbf{1}_{|\tau_i| \le T} \pm T \mathbf{1}_{|\tau_i| > T}$ and corresponding operators $B_N^T(i)$; apply the bounded case, then take $T \to \infty$ using Glivenko's theorem and (5.3) to recover the result.

nodes.name: Theorem 2: Continuous-deformation generalization
nodes.statement: For Hermitian matrices $B_N(n) = A_N + \sum_{k=1}^n \tau(k/n) P_k$ with $P_k$ projections onto i.i.d. unit vectors $q^{(k)}$ and $\tau(t)$ continuous on $[0, 1]$ with $\sup \tau(t) > -1$, conditions I-III imply $\nu(\lambda; B_N(n))$ converges in probability to a limit $\nu(\lambda; c)$ whose Stieltjes transform $u(z, 1)$ is given implicitly by $u(z, t) = z^{-1} w m_0(w)$ with $w = z \exp\big(c \int_0^t \frac{1}{1 - \alpha(\xi)^2 z u(z, \xi)}\, d\xi\big)$ and $\alpha(t) = \tau(t)/(1 + \tau(t))$.
conclusions: Stieltjes transform $u(z, 1)$ satisfies the implicit equation above with unique solution
nodes.notes: Stated without proof in the paper; proof analogous to Theorem 1.

nodes.name: Theorem 3: Random unitary matrices
nodes.statement: For unitary matrices $U_N(n) = V_N \prod_{k=1}^n [(I - P_k) + P_k \exp(i\, \tau(k/n))]$ with $V_N$ a nonrandom unitary, $P_k$ projections onto i.i.d. random unit vectors $q^{(k)}$, and $\tau(t)$ continuous on $[0, 2\pi]$, under conditions I and III the normalized spectral function converges in probability to a limit $\nu(\lambda; c)$ whose associated function $n(z; c) = \int (\lambda - z)^{-1} \ldots$ satisfies a corresponding PDE/implicit equation, with unique solution.
conclusions: Associated transform satisfies a unique-solution PDE/implicit equation analogous to Theorem 1
nodes.notes: Stated without proof. Some details of the integral equation are partially garbled in the OCR text.

nodes.name: Wigner semicircle law (cited)
nodes.statement: For Gaussian Hermitian matrices the limiting normalized spectral density is Wigner's semicircle: $d\nu/d\lambda = \frac{1}{2\pi \sigma^2}\sqrt{4\sigma^2 - \lambda^2}$ supported on $|\lambda| \le 2\sigma$.

nodes.name: Glivenko's theorem (cited)
nodes.statement: For i.i.d. random variables $\tau_i$ with distribution $\sigma(x)$, the empirical distribution function $\sigma(x, T_n)$ converges almost surely to $\sigma(x)$ uniformly on $\mathbb{R}$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.origin_citation: Gnedenko, Course in the theory of probability

nodes.name: Wigner-set similarity
nodes.statement: The set of operators $B_N(n)$ studied is similar to Wigner's set in that as $n \to \infty$ with $n \gg N$ (i.e. $c \to \infty$) the limiting density of Example 1 reduces to the Wigner semicircle, consistent with the central limit theorem for sums of independent random rank-one operators.

nodes.name: Conditions on $A_N$ may be weakened
nodes.statement: Instead of deterministic convergence (II) of $\nu(\lambda; A_N) \to \nu_0(\lambda)$, it suffices to require convergence in probability if $A_N$ is a random operator independent of $\tau_i, q^{(i)}$.

nodes.name: Successive-approximation solution
nodes.statement: The unique solution of the master equation (1.13) can also be obtained by successive approximations, with each iterate having positive imaginary part for $\mathrm{Im}\, z > 0$.
